CLIMATE ACTION 
 
Inaugural Climate Action Plan Adopted  
The 
Elected 
Representatives 
adopted 
the 
Kilkenny County Council Climate Action Plan 
2024-2029 at the Council Plenary on 19th February. 
The Plan sets out how Kilkenny County Council 
will respond to the climate crisis by improving 
energy efficiency, reducing greenhouse gas 
emissions, and embedding climate resilience 
across the organisation. It also addresses how the 
Council will adopt a leadership role in the county 
by supporting local communities, businesses and 
other stakeholders to take climate action.  
 
Welcoming the Plan, Cathaoirleach Cllr Michael 
Doyle said ‘This Plan creates a pathway for Kilkenny 
County Council to reach our climate targets and 
respond to the challenges that climate change poses to 
the county. We look forward to working with all 
stakeholders in its delivery”. 
 
Under the Climate Action and Low Carbon 
Development Act 2021, all local authorities are 
required to prepare a local authority Climate 
Action Plan.  The Plan, which contains 95 actions, 
was adopted following extensive consultation, 
gathering scientific data, and deliberations by the 
Elected Representatives and Staff of Kilkenny 
County Council over the past 12 months.   
 
The Plan’s Vision is that Kilkenny County Council 
will be “A climate resilient organisation that inspires 
and supports the County’s transition to a climate 
resilient, biodiversity rich, sustainable and carbon 
neutral economy by 2050”.

According to Lar Power, Chief Executive “We will continue to build on, and scale up, the achievements of the

€511,00 for community grants in 2024 through the Community Climate Action Fund

€3.5M investment in converting all 12,000 Public Lights to energy efficient LED lights  
▪

▪

Dearbhala Ledwidge, Climate Action Coordinator, says “Thanks to the public, stakeholders, staff and 
Elected Representatives who inputted to the development of the Plan. Every Service Area in the Council 
will commence implementing actions straightaway and we will keep the public informed of progress 
through regular reporting and monitoring.”

ISO 50001 Energy Management System Recertification 
The Council was subject to a 2-day intensive audit of its ISO 50001 energy management system on 5th and 
6th March. An energy management system helps organisations better manage their energy use, thus 
improving productivity. It involves developing and implementing an energy policy, setting achievable 
targets for energy use, and designing action plans to reach them and measure progress. The National 
Climate Action Plan requires all public sector bodies with an energy spend greater than €2 million per 
annum to achieve ISO 50001 certification. Certification is also a requirement to avail of the SEAI Pathfinder 
Funding. We are pleased to confirm that following audit the Council has been recommended for 
recertification under ISO 50001.

The Environmental Awareness Officer (EAO) continues to support 92 schools as part of the An Taisce Green

National Spring Clean 
National Spring Clean is Ireland’s most popular, well recognized and successful anti-litter initiative. Taking 
place during the whole month of April and now in its 25th year, the campaign encourages every sector of 
society to actively participate and take responsibility for litter, by actually conducting clean ups in their 
own local environment. National Spring Clean traditionally takes place throughout the month of April.  
 
National Spring Clean has been operated by An Taisce since 1999 in partnership with the Department of 
Environment, Heritage & Local Government and Local Authorities. 
 
All community and voluntary groups are being encouraged to participate and register with An Taisce via 
About National Spring Clean - National Spring Clean. Groups can request additional supplies from the 
EAO via the Environmental Section. 
 
National Waste Management Plan for a Circular Economy 2024 - 2030 
Ireland is moving away from the traditional linear ‘take-make-use-dispose’ model towards a ‘circular 
economy’ regenerative growth model where resources are reused or recycled as much as possible, and the 
generation of waste is minimized. The transition to a circular economy is essential to reduce pressure on 
natural resources, aid in achieving climate targets, support Sustainable Development Goals and create 
sustainable growth and jobs. 
 
The transition to a circular economy requires a collaborative national response across all sectors of the 
economy through the lifecycle of products and materials. 
 
This Plan covers the period 2024 – 2030.Annual Workplans will be developed for each sector/pillar which 
will coincide with a strategic multi annual workplan which will be developed by a National Coordinating 
Group for Waste and the Circular Economy (NCGWCE).  
 
This committee will consist of the Local Gov Sector, DECC and the EPA so it will afford an opportunity for 
each sector to prioritize separate policy areas/documents. For example, the Climate Action Plan (LG), the 
National Food Waste Prevention Roadmap (DECC) and the National Hazardous Waste Management Plan 
(EPA). National Waste Management Plan for a Circular Economy 2024-2030 - mywaste My Waste

and a further 73 tonnes of dry bulk waste to be transferred for further segregation with a possible 60 – 70% 
of this material being recycled.

The LAIT can play a role in outlining the responsibility the local authority has in integration and the 
coordination/engagement model with the agencies that will support those individuals when a new centre 
opens.  However it’s clear that their role is integration, which does not influence whether a new centre 
opens within area, the profile of those being accommodated and the community engagement prior to that 
centre opening.  
 
The role of the LAIT begins when International Protection Applicants arrive within the County.  The LAITs 
are not responsible for communicating with stakeholder groups and Elected Members ahead of any new 
centre opening. They have no influence or control of these centres, who is due to be accommodated in them, 
or where they are located.  This is the responsibility of DCEDIY.  
 
The LAIT team, consisting of a Integration Co-ordinator and 2 Integration Support Workers, commenced

Currently, there is considerable variation in the provision of integration supports depending on the 
location, the type of accommodation and the availability and accessibility of supports and services in the 
locality. 
 
The Ukrainian Community Forum which has evolved through COVID and the Ukrainian crisis will be 
renamed the ‘Community Integration Forum’ with new terms of reference to ensure wrap around supports 
from all agencies for all the above cohorts.  The Team are currently in the process of meeting with all

information and to eliminate duplication of services. 
 
The role of the LAIT is primarily focused on providing information and signposting to relevant 
stakeholders/key agencies that support. The LAITs will be a key coordination function between the 
individuals, the relevant stakeholders and agencies that support and will use the structure of the 
Community Integration Forum to escalate and manage any issues that are arising.

Kilkenny County Council’s Fire and Rescue Service are obliged under the Fire Services Acts 1981 and 2003

adequately trained and competent to deal with tasks and varying roles they may encounter in the 
performance of their duties. 
 
All personnel responding to Fire and Rescue Service incidents require a minimum level of training to meet 
core requirements.  In addition, many personnel also require further training for specialist or supervisory 
roles.  Furthermore, a number of Fire and Rescue Service personnel have completed Instructor courses in 
order that they in turn can instruct and direct delivery of training sessions / courses.  Personnel also require 
appropriate refresher training in all of the above throughout their careers, generally delivered either 
through on-station training or through specific refresher courses.

and International) and through a variety of arrangements.

firefighters), who have completed the 10-day Using Breathing Apparatus (Initial Wearer) course, with the 
skills, knowledge and competency necessary to wear Breathing Apparatus in compartment fires. 
 
This course is intended to develop the learners in the discharge of their roles as firefighters and to assist 
their Fire Authority in its function as a fire and rescue service. This course provides practical training on 
the knowledge and skills that are required to enable recruit firefighters to safely work as BA wearers at 
operational incidents, within the incident command structure and BA procedural norms.
